title: What will be the open market US Dollar/Iranian Toman exchange rate on December 31, 2026?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the open market US Dollar/Iranian Toman exchange rate on December 31, 2026 (Tehran time). One Toman is equal to 10 Rial.

The primary source for this question will be [Bonbast](https://www.bonbast.com/graph).
fine_print: Iran’s official Central Bank rate will not be used as resolution, only the market rate.
background:
On August 24, 2026, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced [a new round of sanctions on Iran](https://apnews.com/article/iran-rial-currency-bessent-trade-august-24-2026-e367634d8853c8fa4a341132cd577f31) and warned countries to server financial ties with the Islamic Republic. A week earlier President Trump stated he would impose an ["economic D-Day"](https://apnews.com/article/iran-war-trump-sanctions-economic-fury-oil-d28206ea288a3d4a9b82260ab44ce460) on Iran as significant sanctions continue to affect the Iranian regime despite no end to the war.

The ongoing conflict has led to the Iranian Rial to drop to [a historic low of 2.02 million to the US dollar](https://apnews.com/article/iran-rial-currency-bessent-trade-august-24-2026-e367634d8853c8fa4a341132cd577f31) on currency markets. On January 1, 2026, the open market rate was [around 1.35 million Iranian Rial to the US Dollar](https://www.bonbast.com/graph), with a decline of around a third since then.

comments.author: Vlad25
comments.text:
**My forecast: 86.1% chance of exceeding 250,000 toman per USD.**

The Iranian toman has depreciated significantly, with the current open-market exchange rate around 264,000 toman per dollar.

I expect continued inflation, economic sanctions and regional conflict to maintain pressure on the currency through December. Given that the rate has already exceeded 250,000, I believe it is more likely to remain above this level than recover substantially.

However, I've allowed for a roughly 20% chance of a recovery, particularly if diplomatic tensions are eased or the Iranian government successfully intervenes to stabilise the currency.

comments.author: VectorWright
comments.text:
eylonbsh's numbers look right to me. Checked Bonbast myself and the spot rate is sitting around 265k as of Oct 10-11, after hitting an all-time record near 273k on Oct 4 before pulling back a bit. A month earlier, Sept 10, it was only around 234k-235k per the Koboh table below. That's a big move in four weeks, and it already blows through the top of this question's visible 250k range.



tejvn's inflation-parity math is the most rigorous anchor here: spot times (1.86/1.03)^0.25 from an Oct 1 base of 258k lands at 299k, using the 86% annualized Iranian inflation estimate. That's close to eylonbsh's median of 290k, so two independent approaches land in the same neighborhood.



The real counterweight is DeRuina's retracement point and Theomachado's mention of Tehran analysts expecting CBI intervention toward 200-205k. In 2018 and 2020 the free-market rate gave back a quarter to a third of a rapid run-up within weeks once a deal looked plausible, and Polymarket had a 64% chance of a blockade-end announcement by Dec 31 as of Theomachado's Sept 11 check. That's real downside risk, not a rounding error, so I'm not collapsing my lower tail even though the structural inflation story points higher.



Landing at a median of 290k, 265k to 320k interquartile range, under 1% below 150k, and about 88% probability above 250k. Close to eylonbsh's read but with a bit more room on the downside for a diplomatic surprise.

comments.author: tejvn
comments.text:
The community prediction is significantly underestimating the USD/toman rate on December 31 by heavily anchoring to the current spot price. The best estimate is today's spot rate adjusted for the expected inflation gap between Iran and the US. 

#### **Why not interest rate parity?**

The textbook model sets the forward rate from spot using the interest rate gap between the two countries. That model breaks down here. Iran's \~23% nominal rate is set by the government and sits far below inflation, which makes the real rate deeply negative. Because that rate doesn't clear the market, using it would imply only about 4–5% depreciation of the toman through year-end, which isn't plausible. Expected inflation parity is a better anchor.

#### **Inflation Parity**

Iranian inflation has been sticky. It ran at 30–40% through 2023–2025, reached 60% in January 2026, and has averaged roughly 80–90% in the months since the war began ([Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/iran/inflation-cpi)). Even if the blockade is lifted, inflation is likely to stay high through the end of the year.

#### **Why trust spot rate?**

Iran's forex markets have decent volume, so I'm comfortable assuming the current spot rate already prices in public information about the chance of the blockade being lifted. The only adjustment I make is for the drift that inflation implies.

**Calculation**

* Spot: [258k toman/USD](https://alanchand.com/en/currencies-price/usd-hav)
* Expected Iranian inflation: 86% annualized
* Expected US inflation: 3% annualized
* Horizon: t \= 0.25 years (Oct 1 – Dec 31)
* Expected rate \= spot × ((1 + π\_Iran) / (1 + π\_US))^t \= 258k × (1.86 / 1.03)^0.25 ≈ 258k × 1.159 \= **299k.**

comments.author: DeRuina
comments.text: I think the main thing to keep in mind is that the "only one direction" story has a weak track record over three-month windows. In both 2018 and 2020 the free-market rate roughly doubled within months, then gave back a quarter to a third of that move within weeks once a deal or a US political shift looked plausible, before the long-run decline resumed. That retracement pattern matters here because Bonbast's sell rate was already about 235,000 Toman on Sept 27, close to this question's 250,000 upper bound, while Qatar-mediated talks were due to resume this week (NPR, Sept 26). Trend inflation near 66% pushes the rate up steadily — roughly 13% over a quarter, which alone takes 235k to the mid-260s by year-end — but a ceasefire headline could undo months of that in days. That leaves me close to even on whether Dec 31 lands above 250k, with a fat lower tail rather than a thin one. Does anyone have a specific date or catalyst in mind for when Qatar-mediated talks would need to yield a breakthrough to keep the rate under 250,000 by December?

comments.author: tejvn
comments.text: After multiple weeks of the exchange rate hovering between 229k and 238k, the spot exchange rate has risen to 253k, primarily due to Trump rejecting Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. I have shifted my distribution right by 13k, and increased standard deviation by 4%. Source: [https://alanchand.com/en/currencies-price/usd-hav](https://alanchand.com/en/currencies-price/usd-hav) Note that the [official resolution source](https://www.bonbast.com/graph) lags by a few days. comments.author: DaiLothbrook
comments.text: My initial base-rate distribution had a median of 266,500 toman, based on continued depreciation at roughly the recent historical pace. I lowered the center after the exchange rate remained close to 233,600 for several weeks, potentially reflecting central-bank intervention. However, I do not interpret this short plateau as durable stabilization: record lows, sanctions and blockade-related risks still create a meaningful possibility of another sharp depreciation. I therefore use a three-scenario mixture rather than extrapolating one trend. My revised distribution has a 237,500 lower quartile, a 255,100 median and a 280,000 upper quartile, while retaining a relatively heavy upper shock tail.

comments.text:
Let’s take a closer look at the table to see how the current parallel market data flows are shaping up.

The parallel market series shows a 22.39% increase over the last 30 days, with a 30-day high of 237,500 toman.

The 30 day parallel market data show a substantial move upward :



| Date   | USD/IRR   | USD/Toman |
| ------ | --------- | --------- |

| Aug 23 | 1,992,000 | 199,200   |
| Aug 28 | 2,015,000 | 201,500   |
| Sep 1  | 2,159,000 | 215,900   |
| Sep 5  | 2,268,000 | 226,800   |
| Sep 10 | 2,349,000 | 234,900   |
| Sep 12 | 2,338,000 | 233,800   |
| Sep 17 | 2,307,000 | 230,700   |

I don’t think it is reasonable to extrapolate that 22% monthly move indefinitely, however. The recent pullback from 237.5k to around 230.7k shows that intervention and short term stabilization can produce meaningful reversals. That’s why I’m putting my prediction at 247k

250k requires roughly another 21% depreciation from today’s level over the remaining 105 days, or about 5.8% compounded per month. Given the IMF’s 68.9% 2026 inflation projection and -5.4% real-GDP projection, I think that degree of further depreciation is plausible if current pressures persist.

![](https://cdn.metaculus.com/user_uploaded/image_hv31rtX.png)

Picture Source link:

[https://www.imf.org/en/countries/irn](https://www.imf.org/en/countries/irn)

My central case is therefore 247k: continued rial weakness, but not an uncontrolled collapse. The biggest downside risk to this forecast is effective FX intervention or a meaningful improvement in external conditions; the main upside risk is another FX/sanctions shock that pushes the market rapidly through 250k and toward 300k.
